claims.claim_vi: Double-charging a customer is one of the most serious problems a payment system can have; a payment system must guarantee that a payment order is executed exactly once.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Exactly-once is easier if split in two parts: an operation is executed exactly once if it is executed at least once and at the same time at most once; at least once is implemented with retry and at most once with an idempotency check.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Retry: a payment transaction is sometimes retried because of network errors or timeouts; retry provides the at-least-once guarantee; example: a client tries a $10 payment, it keeps failing on a poor connection, and it succeeds at the fourth attempt.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Idempotency: from an API standpoint, clients can make the same call repeatedly and get the same result.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Between clients (web and mobile apps) and servers, an idempotency key is usually a unique value generated by the client that expires after a certain period; a UUID is commonly used, recommended by tech companies such as Stripe and PayPal; the key is added to the HTTP header as idempotency-key: key_value.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: What the server does when it sees a key a second time (return the stored result, ignore the call) is the author's reading of "produce the same result"; the source does not describe it.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against payment-industry documentation.

design_notes_vi: Một khung hai thẻ không nối (hai phần của một đảm bảo, không phải hai bước), một khung hai bước cho thử lại, một khung ghi chú cho khóa chống trùng. Ví dụ 10 đô la lấy từ nguồn.
source_deviations: The source also shows a retry diagram (Figure 10) with four attempts; the lesson keeps the four attempts as two steps (the first three fail, the fourth succeeds).
The source gives the header as idempotency-key: key_value; the lesson writes it as a short phrase and keeps the exact form in the text.
The lesson explains what a repeated call returns as the author's reading, marked as such.
